4.2_same_key_nonce_materials_reuse.conclusion: ALL key-derived material (S, S_inv, pi, a, b, iv_f, iv_b, k_mac, k_kcv) is identical and plaintext-independent under a fixed (key, nonce, dims) tuple. This is a STRUCTURAL fact confirmed both by source inspection (cipher.py:_materials takes no `data` argument) and by direct re-derivation.

4.2_ciphertext_under_reused_key_nonce.note: Despite S/pi/a/b/ivs being completely reused (identical) across P1 and P2, the ciphertext bodies differ almost everywhere, because the chained diffusion (forward then backward, each additive-with-feedback through a fixed but unknown-to-attacker S-box) propagates the single input difference through the whole message. Reuse of S/pi/a/b/ivs is therefore NOT equivalent to 'classical OTP-style keystream reuse': there is no XOR-with-fixed-keystream step whose keystream could be cancelled by XORing two ciphertexts, because diffusion is multiplicative-through-position-dependent-state (additive mod 256 through an S-box), not a simple additive stream cipher. See chosen_plaintext.py for the follow-on structural analysis of exactly what two ciphertexts under reused (key,nonce) DO reveal to an attacker who controls both plaintexts.
